exceptions.reason: The architecture requires full DSL and IUR symmetry, but widget, layering, and theming coverage is still expanding across the ecosystem.
The desktop runtime architecture and platform targets are defined at the ecosystem level, but implementation depth is still evolving.
The desktop runtime is expected to normalize native input into canonical signals, but the SDL2 event bridge is still evolving.

requirements.statement: `unified_ui` shall be the authored DSL boundary for describing ecosystem UIs, widget interactions, and compilation into canonical IUR structures.
`unified_iur` shall be the canonical intermediate exchange format between the DSL and renderer/widget libraries.
Renderer/widget libraries shall treat canonical IUR as the cross-package rendering boundary and shall not require authored DSL modules once IUR is available.
Cross-package UI interaction semantics shall use Jido.Signal values and CloudEvents-compatible event conventions as the shared transport contract.

Introducing or changing canonical DSL surface that affects rendering semantics shall be accompanied by the corresponding `unified_iur` representation change, and vice versa when the IUR addition is intended for canonical DSL authoring.
Every canonical `unified_iur` widget, layout, layering, and theming construct intended for ecosystem-wide authoring shall be representable through the `unified_ui` DSL.
`unified_ui` shall compile authored DSL constructs into canonical `unified_iur` data rather than renderer-specific output formats.
Every DSL entity and attribute intended for canonical rendering shall have a representation in `unified_iur`.
`unified_iur` shall be able to represent widgets, layouts, layering, and theming constructs required by `unified_ui`.
Layering and theming shall remain part of the canonical `unified_ui` DSL surface and shall not be treated as separate authoring systems outside the DSL and IUR symbiosis.
`desktop_ui` shall use canonical Jido.Signal and CloudEvents-compatible semantics inside its own runtime, even when the communication does not leave the desktop package boundary.
`desktop_ui` shall target Windows, macOS, and Linux using an SDL2-based desktop runtime with its own native widget set.
Each widget library shall be able to interpret canonical `unified_iur` input and render it using its own native widget system.
`live_ui` shall use Phoenix LiveView components with JavaScript hooks only where necessary to bridge canonical signals and local widget behavior.
`web_ui` shall use Phoenix for server-side runtime representation and Elm for client-side rendering and local state while preserving canonical IUR and event semantics across the boundary.
Each widget library may expose and evolve its own native widget set independently of the `unified_ui` DSL.
`desktop_ui` shall use the same canonical `Jido.Signal` and CloudEvents-compatible semantics for internal runtime and widget communication, not only for external package boundaries.
`desktop_ui` shall translate native platform input into the same canonical signal contract before events cross package boundaries.
`unified_ui` authored widget interaction bindings shall compile to signal descriptors that can be transported as the canonical event contract.
Ecosystem UI events shall be expressed as `Jido.Signal` values using CloudEvents-compatible semantics.
`live_ui` shall bridge canonical widget events over Phoenix channels using Jido.Signal and CloudEvents semantics while preserving server-authoritative UI behavior.
Renderer-specific local state may vary by library, but cross-package event meanings shall remain canonical at the signal contract boundary.
`web_ui` shall bridge canonical widget events between Phoenix and Elm through CloudEvents-shaped envelopes while preserving canonical event meaning across the boundary.
Cross-cutting governance rationale shall be recorded as ADRs under .spec/decisions/.
Conformance shall be introduced as a separate future layer rather than embedded inside governance contracts.
Durable governance rules shall be authored as Spec Led subjects under .spec/specs/governance/.
Governance artifacts shall capture current enforced policy rather than proposal backlogs or branch-local implementation notes.
Durable cross-cutting governance changes shall add or update at least one ADR under .spec/decisions/ that records context, decision, and consequences.
Governance contracts shall define durable policy and authored obligations, while conformance evidence will be added later in a separate layer.
The .spec workspace shall not grow separate in-flight proposal or branch-local planning folders; Git history and pull requests remain the time dimension for change.
Authored subjects under .spec/specs/**/*.spec.md shall remain the canonical current-truth contract for repository behavior and governance.
A governance subject constrained by a durable ADR shall reference that decision id in spec-meta.decisions.
Durable ecosystem architecture changes shall add or revise an ADR under .spec/decisions/architecture/.

Governance contracts may define required ecosystem invariants before executable conformance artifacts are introduced, but they shall not imply conformance coverage exists before the dedicated conformance layer is authored.
Governance changes shall preserve the distinction between authored DSL semantics, canonical IUR, and native widget-library implementations unless an ADR explicitly redefines that boundary.
Changes to package responsibilities, DSL and IUR mapping, or signal transport shall update the affected ecosystem subject specs in the same change set.
Repository-wide governance contracts and ADRs shall apply across all packages unless a subject spec explicitly narrows scope.
The repository shall keep implementation packages under packages/ while repository-wide governance remains centralized in the root .spec workspace.
The repository shall keep a single canonical .spec/ workspace at the repository root for repository-wide governance and package-level intent.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that gives local operating guidance for agents working inside the .spec workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/decisions/README.md that explains when durable ADRs belong in the workspace.
The workspace shall define a governance layer under .spec/specs/governance/ for durable repository-wide contracts and policies.
The repository shall include a .spec/README.md that explains purpose, layout, and workflow.
The repository shall author subject specs under .spec/specs/**/*.spec.md so nested layers such as governance remain parser-compatible without custom rules.
Durable ADRs may be organized under nested paths below .spec/decisions/ and shall remain valid Spec Led decision documents.
When planning and verification run, the workspace shall generate .spec/state.json containing indexed subjects, indexed decisions, and verification state across the authored specs and ADR trees.
The adapter layer shall coordinate platform detection, renderer selection, multi-platform rendering, and signal routing across the terminal, desktop, and web adapters implemented by the package.
The package shall provide adapter-side event normalization and dispatch helpers that convert platform events or element metadata into runtime-dispatchable signals.
The package shall define a renderer behaviour with `render/2`, `update/3`, and `destroy/1` callbacks over IUR trees and renderer-owned state.
The adapter layer shall validate event actions and payloads, sanitize user-provided data, and redact sensitive fields before renderer-driven dispatch uses that data.
The adapter layer shall expose shared pure utilities for IUR traversal, style and id inspection, and renderer state bookkeeping used across renderers.
DSL compilation shall verify unique ids, valid label references, and supported signal handler formats before a module is accepted.
The DSL shall support state-backed attribute values and preserve runtime state context through compile indexing and view building.
The package shall expose introspection helpers that return compiled widgets, layouts, styles, and supported signals for a DSL module or DSL state.
The package shall provide a Spark-based DSL that compiles module-body UI declarations into the generated component surface expected by `UnifiedUi` modules.
The DSL layer shall expose standard signal names and helper utilities for shaping and validating handler payloads used by authored UI modules.
The DSL shall support named styles and themes alongside inline style data and resolve them during IUR construction.

`packages/unified-ui` shall publish itself as the `:unified_ui` library and declare the current multi-platform DSL, renderer, signal, and `unified_iur`-facing package metadata in its package manifest and top-level module.
The package OTP application shall start the PubSub, registry, and dynamic supervisor infrastructure needed by the current signal bus and component agent runtime.
The component server runtime shall batch pending signals, flush them into model updates, and rebuild current IUR and render results on demand.
The runtime shall support starting, locating, querying, signaling, rendering, and stopping supervised component processes by component id.
The package shall define an Elm-style component behaviour with `init/1`, `update/2`, and `view/1` callbacks over map-shaped model state, `Jido.Signal` inputs, and IUR outputs.

The runtime shall degrade safely when initialization, update, topic subscription, or process lifecycle operations fail by returning fallback state or explicit runtime errors rather than crashing callers.
The package shall provide standard signal creation and validation helpers together with a PubSub-backed signal bus for broadcasting normalized `Jido.Signal` values.
The package shall provide generator tasks for current extension points, including `mix unified_ui.gen.widget`, `mix unified_ui.gen.screen`, and `mix unified_ui.gen.extension`.
The package shall provide current workflow wrapper tasks for formatting, testing, benchmarking, and performance checks.
The package shall provide project inspection and preview tasks that can render screen modules across supported platforms and report codebase statistics.
The package shall provide `mix unified_ui.new` to scaffold a new UnifiedUi project with a starter screen, application, tests, and baseline project files.

The current package shall support the implemented higher-level input, container, specialized, and monitoring entities including pick lists, form builders, viewports, split panes, canvas, command palettes, log viewers, stream widgets, and process monitors.
The current package shall support foundational authored widgets and layouts including text, button, label, text_input, vbox, hbox, grid, stack, and zbox.
The current IUR builder shall translate supported DSL entities into `UnifiedIUR` or package-defined element structs while resolving styles and runtime state references.
The current package shall support data visualization and tabular authored entities including gauge, sparkline, bar_chart, line_chart, table, and column.
The current package shall support navigation and feedback authored entities including menu, context_menu, tabs, tree_view, dialog, alert_dialog, toast, and their related child entities.

meta.summary: High-level architecture contract for the DSL, the canonical IUR, the renderer/widget libraries, and the shared event transport.
Symbiotic contract between authored DSL entities in `unified_ui` and canonical widget, layout, layering, and theming representation in `unified_iur`.
Architecture contract for `web_ui`, `live_ui`, and `desktop_ui` as native widget libraries that also consume canonical IUR.
Shared Jido.Signal and CloudEvents-compatible transport contract across the DSL, IUR consumers, and renderer runtimes.
Governance contract for changes to package responsibilities, DSL and IUR boundaries, and cross-package signal transport.
Normative governance contract for authored subjects, ADR use, and durable repository-wide policy changes.
Repository-wide governance layer for durable contracts, ADR-backed policy, and future separation from conformance.
Repository-level specification for the unified monorepo and its centralized spec workspace.
Canonical workspace contract for authored specs, governance subjects, ADRs, and generated Spec Led state.
Current adapter-layer contract for `packages/unified-ui`, derived from the implemented renderer, coordinator, event, shared-state, and security modules.
Current Spark-based DSL contract for `packages/unified-ui`, derived from the package implementation and tests.
Current codebase-derived contract for the `packages/unified-ui` library, its published package metadata, and its OTP runtime support.
Current runtime contract for `packages/unified-ui`, derived from the implemented Elm behaviour, signal helpers, bus, and agent runtime.
Current Mix-task tooling contract for `packages/unified-ui`, derived from the implemented project scaffolding, generators, preview utilities, and developer workflow wrappers.
Current supported widget, layout, and builder surface for `packages/unified-ui`, derived from the package implementation.
